Messages.Body:
I accidentally bought some conscripted statues, so now I have 17 and
need to find a way to use (abuse) them.
I assume you can play a freak drive after having played the statue if
you play it at superior? (After the combat with the ally).

Freak Drive, Action Modifier, 1 blood, Fortitude, R2/R , [Jyhad:R2,
V:TES:R, CE:U/PV2, Anarchs:PG]
[for] Only usable at the end of a successful action (after resolving
the action). Untap this vampire. [FOR] As above, but usable even if
the action is blocked (play after combat, if any).

Conscripted Statue, Action Modifier, Visceratika, R2 , [Bloodlines:R2]
Only usable when an action is blocked. [vis] The opposing minion takes
1 damage during strike resolution each round of the resulting combat
if range is close. [VIS] Combat does not occur. Put this card into
play. This card represents an ally with 2 life and 2 strength. This
ally enters combat with the blocking minion. This ally gets 1 optional
press during the combat. Burn this card at the end of combat or if the
combat is canceled.

Messages.Author: Johannes Walch
Messages.Body:
niko...@hotmail.com schrieb:

> I accidentally bought some conscripted statues, so now I have 17 and
> need to find a way to use (abuse) them.
> I assume you can play a freak drive after having played the statue if
> you play it at superior? (After the combat with the ally).

Yes you can play Freak Drive. If an action modifier or a reaction card
ends the action it is specifically noted in the card text, e.g from
Obedience "and end the current action (and combat)".

--
Johannes Walch

Well, I am thinking of a multiacting gargoyle deck. Lots of different
actions, mostly retainers and equipment that boosts bleed. If people
block when you are equipping, they end up fighting the ally and take 4
dam (assuming no cards being played) after which you untap and do
another action. (Lear jet will give you the option of flushing the
statues when people stop blocking you and the beauty of it is that the
freak drives will just be used normally then).
And yes, a memories of mortality played on someone who tends to block
alot combined with a few traps, will definitely make people think
twice about blocking... :)

Making the deck later today.
